text.p: Australian gold miner Continental Goldfields Ltd said on Thursday it had acquired 24.3 percent or 63.9 million shares of South African gold producer Knights Gold Mining Co Ltd for 25.6 million rand or A$7.22 million.
Knights produces 50,000 ounces of gold annually, primarily from the retreatment of tailings dumps located adjacent to Johannesburg, Continental Goldfields said.
The South African miner has reserves of 84 million tonnes of retreatable material within its dumps equating to 1.4 million ounces of contained gold, Continental said.
Knights owns and operates a processing plant with a capacity in excess of three million tonnes per annum.
Economic mine-life of the present dumps at current extraction rates is in excess of 13 years, Continental said.
Continental said Knights other major shareholder is Dundee Bank Corp Inc./N.W. Goodman and Company of Toronto, Canada, which holds about 27 percent of Knight.
"This transaction is consistent with Continental's stated objective of becoming a significant gold producer/investor in South Africa," Continental said.

Continential said the move would bring a positive cash flow to current operations and had the potential to fund exploration activities associated with the company's investment in Transvaal Gold Mining Estates Ltd.
"Continental believes that there is potential to expand the operations of Knights thereby enhancing future profits with the attendant increase in return to shareholders," it said.
Continental shares closed one cent up at 22 cents.
